messages:
Leah Ortiz: Heads-up from Support (SR-4892). Customer on Dedicated (NA-west-3-dedicated-1) seeing p95 jump after we flipped a new quant profile 'fp8_aggressive' for redwood-open-7b. p50 steady. They say p99 is unpredictable up to ~2.2s.
Samir Rao: Which profile settings landed? fp8_aggressive had calibration_samples=2048, per_op fallback default, mixed-precision allowed, and fast-kernel preference on Ampere.
Marta Varga: We enabled fp8 kernels + fallback mixing last night during the rolling config push. Noticed a few warnings in the fleet logs earlier.
Toby: Any evidence of cross-precision penalties? e.g., memcpy or dtype conversion hotspots?
Marta Varga: Yes. Sample from node logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T02:12:01Z] WARN quant: calibration_confidence low for layer 37 -> mark mixed
[2026-03-15T02:12:01Z] INFO kernel: using fp8 for 90 ops, fp16 for 38 ops
[2026-03-15T02:12:02Z] WARN runtime: dtype-conversion stall 312ms on thread 4
[2026-03-15T02:12:03Z] ERROR runtime: request latency 2210ms (fallback conversions + kv-cache refill)
```
Leah Ortiz: Customer load profile: 50-200 rps, many short-turn prompts (avg 40 tokens). They depend on tight tails for interactive UI.
Samir Rao: fp8 gives better throughput but is more sensitive to calibration since dynamic range is tighter. If the calibration dataset didn't match short-turn prompts, ops will flip to fp16 and cause conversions.
Toby: Do we have observability for "per-request precision plan"? Want to see whether individual requests are mixing.
Marta Varga: We emit quant.plan per request but it's sampled at 1%. We can bump sampling to 100% for that customer's pool for diagnostics.
Leah Ortiz: Customer requested a mitigation they can flip ASAP. They don't want a full rollback yet.
Samir Rao: Options we can offer: 
- Toggle: quantization.fallback_policy=per-request (forces whole request to fp16 when confidence low)
- Toggle: quantization.allow_mixed=false (force all ops to be fp8 or fp16 only)
- Rollback to 'fp16_stable' profile (no quant)
- Run a tailored recalibration using their sampled prompts (they can share ~3k prompts)
Toby: Per-request fallback seems best: trades some median latency for a much better tail. If we do per-request we must warm the kv-cache for that path.
Marta Varga: Re-calibration plan: run 10k steps with their prompts + augmentations, then produce a confidence map per-layer. If confidence >= 0.9 keep fp8; else mark layer forced-fp16. That reduces mixed layers.
Samir Rao: Quick repro in our perf cluster: 
```bash
# repro harness
./bench_client --model redwood-open-7b --profile fp8_aggressive \ 
  --workload customer_short_turns.json --concurrency 16 --tokens 40
```
Results: p50 ~95ms, p95 ~420ms (mixed), p95 ~120ms when forcing per-request fp16 fallback after warmup, fp16-only p95 ~110ms.
Leah Ortiz: Action plan: 
1) Increase quant.plan sampling to 100% for NA-west-3-dedicated-1 (diagnostics) -> Marta
2) Offer customer quick toggle to quantization.fallback_policy=per-request -> Samir to flip (no code change).
3) Ask customer for 3k representative prompts for recalibration -> Leah to request.
4) Start recalibration job with augmented set and produce layer confidence report -> Marta.
5) Add telemetry alert: if p95 increases >25% within 30m after profile change, auto-revert -> Toby.
Samir Rao: I'll flip the per-request fallback on their pool now and set warmup_requests=1500 so the runtime preloads the KV cache.
support-bot: Customer notified: "We've enabled a per-request fallback on your dedicated pool and are running warmup. Please let us know if you still see high tail latency."
deploy-bot: Rolling update: quant.fallback_policy=per-request applied to NA-west-3-dedicated-1 (targeting 12 nodes). Monitoring for 20m.
Marta Varga: Increased sampling for quant.plan on the affected pool. Early telemetry shows mixed->per-request cut the p99 incidents by ~70% after warmup.
Toby: Important note: mixed-precision conversions introduce not just conversion cost but also KV cache fragmentation: when ops change dtype, KV cache entries may be stored differently causing misses. Warmup reduces this.
Leah Ortiz: Customer replied: after the toggle p95 dropped to ~140ms and p99 to ~320ms. They're OK with this while we run recalibration.
Samir Rao: Follow-ups: 
- Make per-deployment quotas for quant.plan sampling so we can do targeted debug without noise.
- Add preflight check in console before applying aggressive quant profile: show expected confidence and required calibration size.
- Document 'warmup_requests' recommendations per profile (fp8 needs higher warmup).
Toby: I'll file a short RFC for a runtime change: 'prefer-homogeneous-execution' option that ensures single-precision execution per request if mixing would exceed a threshold. This can be auto-enabled when tail-sensitive label is set on deployment.
Marta Varga: Scheduling recalibration job now. Will post layer confidence details and a patch to the profile to reduce mixed layers.
Leah Ortiz: Owners: Marta -> recalibration + telemetry sampling, Samir -> customer toggle + comms, Toby -> alert and RFC, Leah -> tracking with Support. Keeping this thread as SR-4892 source of truth.
Marta Varga: Update: after a 6k sample recalibration, we forced 12 layers to fp16 and the rest stayed fp8. New perf: p95 ~130ms, p99 ~280ms. Pushing recommended profile to their pool next maintenance window unless they ask for immediate.
support-bot: SR-4892 updated: customer accepted recommended profile change scheduled for next window.
Leah Ortiz: Closing notes for postmortem: 
- Require representative prompt set before aggressive quant profile rollout to dedicated pools
- Default quantization.fallback_policy should be reviewable per-deployment via Console
- Add KPI gate: block profile rollout if sampled quant_confidence per-layer < 0.85
Thanks all.
